1→---
     2→layout: page
     3→title: Boot Sequence
     4→permalink: /boot-sequence/
     5→---
     6→
     7→# KN5000 Boot Sequence
     8→
     9→This page documents the complete boot sequence of the Technics KN5000, from power-on to a fully functional system. The KN5000 uses a dual-CPU architecture where the Main CPU orchestrates startup and loads firmware to the Sub CPU.
    10→
    11→> **See Also**: [System Overview]({{ site.baseurl }}/system-overview/) for overall architecture and [CPU Subsystem]({{ site.baseurl }}/cpu-subsystem/) for detailed CPU specifications.
    12→
    13→## Overview
    14→
    15→```
    16→Power On
    17→    │
    18→    ▼
    19→┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
    20→│   Main CPU      │     │    Sub CPU      │
    21→│  TMP94C241F     │     │   TMP94C241F    │
    22→│  (IC10)         │     │   (IC27)        │
    23→└────────┬────────┘     └────────┬────────┘
    24→         │                       │
    25→         │  1. Table Data ROM    │  1. Boot ROM
    26→         │     First-stage boot  │     0xFF8290
    27→         │                       │
    28→         ▼                       ▼
    29→    Memory Remap            Init Hardware
    30→    Program ROM → 0xE00000  Wait for payload
    31→         │                       │
    32→         │  2. Program ROM       │
    33→         │     RESET_HANDLER     │
    34→         │                       │
    35→         ▼                       ▼
    36→    Init Hardware           Receive payload
    37→    Load Sub CPU            at 0x0400
    38→    Payload (192KB)              │
    39→         │                       │
    40→         │   ◄─── DMA ───►       │
    41→         │   (0x120000 latch)    │
    42→         │                       │
    43→         ▼                       ▼
    44→    Start Subsystems        Execute Payload
    45→    (UI, MIDI, FDC...)      (Audio Engine)
    46→         │                       │
    47→         ▼                       ▼
    48→    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
    49→    │     System Ready            │
    50→    └─────────────────────────────┘
    51→```
    52→
    53→## Main CPU Boot Sequence
    54→
    55→### Discovery: Two-Stage Boot Process
    56→
    57→**Important finding**: The Main CPU uses a **two-stage boot process**. On reset, the **Table Data ROM** is initially mapped at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF and contains a first-stage bootloader. This bootloader configures the memory controller to remap the Program ROM to 0xE00000, then jumps to the main firmware.
    58→
    59→### Stage 1: Table Data ROM Bootloader
    60→
    61→> **Status**: The table_data boot code section (0xFFB4E8-0xFFFFFF, 19,224 bytes) is now **100% byte-matching**. See `table_data/kn5000_table_data.asm` and the reference disassembly at `original_ROMs/table_data_bootcode.unidasm`.
    62→
    63→#### Reset Vector (0xFFFEE0)
    64→
    65→On CPU reset, the Table Data ROM is mapped at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF. The reset vector at 0xFFFEE0 (table_data offset 0x1FFEE0) contains:
    66→
    67→```asm
    68→JP 0x00FFB4E8    ; Jump to first-stage boot code
    69→```
    70→
    71→#### First-Stage Boot Code (0xFFB4E8)
    72→
    73→The table_data bootloader at 0xFFB4E8 performs critical memory controller configuration:
    74→
    75→```asm
    76→; Memory Start Address Registers - define where each block appears
    77→LD (MSAR0), 0x1E    ; Block 0 → 0x1E0000 (SRAM)
    78→LD (MSAR1), 0x10    ; Block 1 → 0x100000 (I/O)
    79→LD (MSAR2), 0xC0    ; Block 2 → 0xC00000
    80→LD (MSAR3), 0x00    ; Block 3 → 0x000000 (DRAM)
    81→LD (MSAR4), 0x80    ; Block 4 → 0x800000 (Table Data - NEW location)
    82→LD (MSAR5), 0x00    ; Block 5 → 0x000000
    83→
    84→; Memory Address Mask Registers - define block sizes
    85→LD (MAMR0), 0x0F    ; Block 0 mask
    86→LD (MAMR1), 0x3F    ; Block 1 mask
    87→LD (MAMR2), 0x7F    ; Block 2 mask
    88→LD (MAMR3), 0x1F    ; Block 3 mask
    89→LD (MAMR4), 0xFF    ; Block 4 mask
    90→LD (MAMR5), 0xFF    ; Block 5 mask
    91→
    92→; DRAM Controller initialization
    93→LD (DRAM1REF), 0x81
    94→LD (DRAM1CRL), 0x8B
    95→LD (DRAM1CRH), 0x58
    96→LD (PMEMCR), 0xF1
    97→```
    98→
    99→After this configuration:
   100→- **Table Data ROM** is remapped to 0x800000-0x9FFFFF
   101→- **Program ROM** becomes visible at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF
   102→- The bootloader jumps to the Program ROM's `RESET_HANDLER` at 0xEF03C6
   103→
   104→#### Boot_ClearRAM Routine (0xFFB740)
   105→
   106→The first-stage bootloader calls `Boot_ClearRAM` to initialize RAM and copy essential data from ROM:
   107→
   108→```asm
   109→Boot_ClearRAM:
   110→    ; Clear 35,146 bytes at RAM 0x104E (general RAM area)
   111→    LD XDE, 0x0000104E    ; Destination
   112→    LD XBC, 0x0000894A    ; Count
   113→    ; Uses LDIRW for efficient word-mode fill with zeros
   114→
   115→    ; Clear 1,091 bytes at RAM 0x0C00 (boot variables)
   116→    LD XDE, 0x00000C00
   117→    LD XBC, 0x00000443
   118→
   119→    ; Copy 10 bytes from ROM 0xFFB4D2 to RAM 0x1044
   120→    ; Data: 00 40 20 08 10 04 02 00 01 00 (bit mask table)
   121→
   122→    ; Copy 12 bytes from ROM 0xFFB4DC to RAM 0x9998
   123→    ; Data: 7E 00 10 00 00 00 80 00 00 00 00 00 (init params)
   124→```
   125→
   126→The bit mask table at 0x1044 is used for bit manipulation operations throughout the firmware. The initialization parameters at 0x9998 appear to be related to stack/display setup.
   127→
   128→#### Flash Programming Routines (0xFFB812-0xFFC8C1)
   129→
   130→The bootloader contains a complete set of flash programming routines for all target memories:
   131→
   132→| Routine Type | Address Range | Targets |
   133→|--------------|---------------|---------|
   134→| 16-bit flash routines | 0xFFB812-0xFFBC1C | HDAE5000 ROM, Custom Data Flash |
   135→| 32-bit flash routines | 0xFFBC1D-0xFFC0D2 | Table Data ROM (interleaved) |
   136→| Disk detection | 0xFFBFC4-0xFFC0D2 | Floppy disk header validation |
   137→
   138→> **See Also**: [Flash Programming]({{ site.baseurl }}/flash-programming/) for detailed protocol documentation and comparison with Program ROM flash routines.
   139→
   140→#### LZSS Decompressor Suite (0xFFC8C2-0xFCCA4F)
   141→
   142→The bootloader includes a complete LZSS decompression subsystem for handling compressed firmware data. This is the "SLIDE4K" format used by the firmware update system.
   143→
   144→> **Status**: All LZSS routines (872 bytes total) are now **100% byte-matching** disassembly in `table_data/kn5000_table_data.asm`.
   145→
   146→##### Decompressor Routines
   147→
   148→| Routine | Address | Size | Purpose |
   149→|---------|---------|------|---------|
   150→| `LZSS_ReadByte` | 0xFFC8C2 | 115 bytes | Read from compressed stream with sector buffering |
   151→| `LZSS_OutputByte` | 0xFFC935 | 63 bytes | Write decompressed bytes with 32-bit batching |
   152→| `LZSS_OutputByte_Alt` | 0xFFC974 | 63 bytes | Alternative output for flash update mode |
   153→| `LZSS_ParseHeader` | 0xFFC9B3 | 157 bytes | Parse/validate firmware header, setup source |
   154→| `LZSS_Decompress` | 0xFFCA50 | 474 bytes | Main decompression loop with sliding window |
   155→
   156→##### Format Characteristics
   157→
   158→| Parameter | Value | Description |
   159→|-----------|-------|-------------|
   160→| Window Size | 4096 bytes (0x1000) | Standard SLIDE4K |
   161→| Pre-fill | 0x00 for first 4078 bytes | Window positions 0-0x0FED |
   162→| Initial Position | 0x0FEE | First write position |
   163→| Offset Bits | 12 bits | Masked with 0x0FFF |
   164→| Length Bits | 4 bits | Stored in high nibble of second byte |
   165→| Flag Byte | High bit = sentinel | Bit 0: 1=literal, 0=back-ref |
   166→| Header | "SLIDE4K" + size | 11+ byte header with magic and decompressed size |
   167→
   168→##### RAM Variables (0x0C20-0x0C38)
   169→
   170→| Address | Name | Purpose |
   171→|---------|------|---------|
   172→| 0x0C20 | Expected Size | Target decompressed size (3 bytes LE) |
   173→| 0x0C24 | Output Position | Current output byte count |
   174→| 0x0C28 | Dest Address | Destination pointer for decompressed data |
   175→| 0x0C2C | Buffer Pointer | Sector read buffer (typically 0x0099A4) |
   176→| 0x0C30 | Display X | Progress indicator X coordinate |
   177→| 0x0C32 | Display Y | Progress indicator Y coordinate |
   178→| 0x0C34 | Sector Offset | Current sector read offset |
   179→| 0x0C36 | Byte Counter | Output byte counter (0-3 for 32-bit writes) |
   180→| 0x0C38 | Source Address | Compressed data source pointer |
   181→
   182→##### Decompression Algorithm
   183→
   184→```
   185→1. Allocate 4KB window buffer (via malloc at 0xFFFB56)
   186→2. Pre-fill window[0..0xFED] with 0x00
   187→3. Set window_pos = 0x0FEE
   188→4. Read 8-byte header, then 3-byte size (little-endian)
   189→5. Main Loop:
   190→   a. Shift flag byte right
   191→   b. If bit 8 clear, read new flag byte (set bit 8 as sentinel)
   192→   c. If bit 0 = 1: read literal byte, output to dest and window
   193→   d. If bit 0 = 0:
   194→      - Read offset low byte (8 bits)
   195→      - Read offset high + length byte
   196→      - Offset = (high_nibble << 8) | low_byte (12 bits)
   197→      - Length = low_nibble + 2
   198→      - Copy (length) bytes from window[offset] to output
   199→   e. Update window_pos (masked to 12 bits)
   200→6. Continue until output_size reached
   201→7. Free window buffer (via free at 0xFFFCDD)
   202→```
   203→
   204→##### Compressed Data Locations
   205→
   206→| Location | Address | Contents | Header |
   207→|----------|---------|----------|--------|
   208→| **Table Data ROM** | 0x8E0000 | Compressed parameter data (~33KB) | `"SLIDE4K", 0x00, 0x00, 0x95...` |
   209→| **Boot Headers** | 0x9FA000 | Update file type signatures | `"SLIDE"` markers |
   210→| **Boot UI** | 0x9FA150 | Flash update UI bitmaps | `"SLIDE"` marker + bitmap |
   211→
   212→**Note:** The data at 0x8E0000 does NOT contain the Sub CPU executable. See [Subprogram Storage Location](#subprogram-storage-location-under-investigation) below.
   213→
   214→##### Callers of LZSS Decoder
   215→
   216→The LZSS decoder is invoked during flash firmware updates:
   217→
   218→| Routine | Address | File Type | Source |
   219→|---------|---------|-----------|--------|
   220→| `HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h` | 0xEF47FA | Program DATA FILE PCK | 0x3E0000, 0x3F0000 |
   221→| `HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_008h` | 0xEF481E | Table DATA FILE PCK | Table Data ROM |
   222→| `LZSS_ParseHeader` | 0xFFC9B3 | Flash update mode | 0x3E0000 (boot context) |
   223→
   224→##### Update File Types
   225→
   226→The firmware update system recognizes these LZSS-compressed file types:
   227→
   228→| ID | File Type String | Description |
   229→|----|-----------------|-------------|
   230→| 0x07 | `"Technics KN5000 Program  DATA FILE PCK"` | Compressed program ROM |
   231→| 0x08 | `"Technics KN5000 Table    DATA FILE PCK"` | Compressed table data |
   232→| - | `"Technics KN5000 CMPCUSTOMDATA FILE"` | Compressed custom data |
   233→
   234→The `PCK` suffix indicates LZSS-compressed content using the SLIDE4K format.
   235→
   236→#### Evidence
   237→
   238→The table_data ROM contains a complete interrupt vector table at offset 0x1FFF00:
   239→
   240→| Vector | Address | Target | Description |
   241→|--------|---------|--------|-------------|
   242→| 0 (Reset) | 0xFFFEE0 | 0xFFB4E8 | First-stage boot code |
   243→| 1-7 | 0xFFB705 | Handler | Common interrupt handler |
   244→| 11 | 0xFFEAB2 | Handler | Specific handler |
   245→
   246→The memory controller values in the table_data bootloader are **identical** to those in the Program ROM boot code (lines 134224-134235 of `kn5000_v10_program.asm`), confirming this is the intended configuration.
   247→
   248→### Stage 2: Program ROM Main Boot
   249→
   250→#### Reset Handler (0xEF03C6)
   251→
   252→After memory remapping, execution continues at `RESET_HANDLER` in the Program ROM. The TMP94C241F CPU now sees the Program ROM at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF.
   253→
   254→#### Hardware Initialization
   255→
   256→The reset handler performs additional hardware setup (note: memory controller is already configured by Stage 1):
   257→
   258→| Step | Description | Key Registers |
   259→|------|-------------|---------------|
   260→| 1 | Disable watchdog | WDMOD, WDCR |
   261→| 2 | Configure clock | CLKMOD |
   262→| 3 | Initialize ports | P0-PZ, PxCR, PxFC |
   263→| 4 | Set up memory controller | MSARx, MAMRx, BxCS |
   264→| 5 | Initialize DRAM | DREFCR, DMEMCR |
   265→| 6 | Configure timers | T01MOD, T4MOD, etc. |
   266→| 7 | Initialize stack | XSP = stack address |
   267→
   268→#### Sub CPU Payload Loading
   269→
   270→After hardware initialization, the main CPU loads a 192KB firmware payload to the sub CPU via DMA through the inter-CPU latch at `0x140000` (main CPU side) / `0x120000` (sub CPU side).
   271→
   272→> **Deep Dive: Sub CPU Payload Transfer**
   273→>
   274→> The payload transfer is handled by `SubCPU_Send_Payload` (0xEF068A) using the E1 bulk transfer protocol. This is one of the most complex boot operations, involving:
   275→> - Multiple 64KB chunk transfers from Table Data ROM
   276→> - Optional LZSS decompression of preset data
   277→> - Careful timing with delay loops
   278→>
   279→> **Quick Reference:**
   280→> - [`SubCPU_Send_Payload`](#subcpu_send_payload-details) - Main transfer routine (see below)
   281→> - [Inter-CPU Protocol]({{ site.baseurl }}/inter-cpu-protocol/#subcpu_send_payload-0xef068a) - Full technical details with code examples
   282→> - [Open Questions](#sub-cpu-payload-transfer---open-questions) - Disputed interpretations about destination addresses
   283→
   284→**Main CPU Boot Sequence:**
   285→```
   286→RESET_HANDLER (0xEF03C6)
   287→    │
   288→    ├── LD (PA), 0xFE         ; Hold Sub CPU in reset (bit 0 = 0)
   289→    │
   290→    ├── ... hardware init ...
   291→    │
   292→    ├── SET 0, (PA)           ; Release Sub CPU from reset (0xEF05F3)
   293→    │
   294→    ├── CALL SubCPU_Init_DMA_Channels  ; Set up DMA at 0xEF329E
   295→    │
   296→    ├── EI 0                  ; Enable interrupts
   297→    │
   298→    └── CALR SubCPU_Send_Payload       ; Send 192KB payload at 0xEF068A
   299→```
   300→
   301→**E1 Transfer Protocol Summary:**
   302→1. Main CPU waits for SSTAT1 high (Sub CPU ready)
   303→2. Main CPU sends E1 command byte (0xE1) to latch
   304→3. Main CPU sends 6-byte header (destination address + byte count)
   305→4. Main CPU sends actual data via DMA
   306→5. Repeat for each 64KB chunk
   307→6. Sub CPU receives E3 command, sets bit 6 of PAYLOAD_LOADED_FLAG
   308→7. Sub CPU boot ROM calls payload at 0x000400
   309→
   310→See [Inter-CPU Protocol]({{ site.baseurl }}/inter-cpu-protocol/) for detailed protocol documentation.
   311→
   312→#### Subsystem Initialization
   313→
   314→After the sub CPU payload is loaded:
   315→
   316→| Subsystem | Description |
   317→|-----------|-------------|
   318→| Display | VGA-compatible LCD controller at 0x1A0000 |
   319→| Control Panel | Serial communication with MCU (SC1, 250kHz) |
   320→| FDC | Floppy disk controller at 0x110000 |
   321→| MIDI | External MIDI I/O |
   322→| HDAE5000 | Hard disk expansion (if present) at 0x160000 |
   323→
   324→#### Main Loop
   325→
   326→The main CPU enters its event loop, handling:
   327→- User interface events
   328→- Control panel button/encoder input
   329→- MIDI I/O
   330→- Disk operations
   331→- Display updates
   332→
   333→### Complete Boot Flow Diagram
   334→
   335→```
   336→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   337→│                         POWER ON / RESET                              │
   338→│                                                                       │
   339→│  Initial Memory Map:                                                  │
   340→│    0xE00000-0xFFFFFF = Table Data ROM (contains first-stage boot)    │
   341→│    Program ROM not yet visible                                        │
   342→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   343→                                   │
   344→                                   ▼
   345→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   346→│                   STAGE 1: TABLE DATA BOOTLOADER                      │
   347→│                                                                       │
   348→│  1. CPU fetches reset vector from 0xFFFF00 (table_data @ 0x1FFF00)   │
   349→│  2. Vector points to 0xFFFEE0 → JP 0xFFB4E8                          │
   350→│  3. Boot code configures MSAR0-5, MAMR0-5, DRAM controller           │
   351→│  4. Memory remap: Table Data → 0x800000, Program ROM → 0xE00000      │
   352→│  5. Jump to Program ROM entry point (0xEF03C6)                        │
   353→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   354→                                   │
   355→                                   ▼
   356→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   357→│                    STAGE 2: PROGRAM ROM BOOT                          │
   358→│                                                                       │
   359→│  Final Memory Map:                                                    │
   360→│    0x000000-0x0FFFFF = DRAM (1MB)                                    │
   361→│    0x100000-0x1FFFFF = I/O (FDC, latches, VGA, SRAM)                 │
   362→│    0x300000-0x3FFFFF = Custom Data Flash                              │
   363→│    0x400000-0x7FFFFF = Rhythm Data ROM                                │
   364→│    0x800000-0x9FFFFF = Table Data ROM (remapped)                      │
   365→│    0xE00000-0xFFFFFF = Program ROM (now visible)                      │
   366→│                                                                       │
   367→│  1. RESET_HANDLER at 0xEF03C6                                         │
   368→│  2. Hardware initialization (redundant memory controller setup)       │
   369→│  3. Release Sub CPU from reset                                        │
   370→│  4. Send 192KB payload to Sub CPU                                     │
   371→│  5. Initialize subsystems and enter main loop                         │
   372→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   373→```
   374→
   375→### Implications for MAME Emulation
   376→
   377→The discovery of the two-stage boot process has significant implications for accurate MAME emulation:
   378→
   379→#### Current Driver (Incorrect)
   380→
   381→The current MAME driver uses a static memory map:
   382→```cpp
   383→map(0x800000, 0x9fffff).rom().region("table_data", 0);
   384→map(0xe00000, 0xffffff).rom().region("program", 0);
   385→```
   386→
   387→This assumes the Program ROM is always at 0xE00000, which is only true **after** the memory controller is configured.
   388→
   389→#### Required Fix
   390→
   391→For accurate emulation, the MAME driver needs to:
   392→
   393→1. **On reset**: Map Table Data ROM at 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF
   394→2. **Emulate MSAR/MAMR register writes**: When the bootloader writes to memory controller registers (0x0142-0x0157), update the address mapping dynamically
   395→3. **After reconfiguration**: Program ROM becomes visible at 0xE00000, Table Data at 0x800000
   396→
   397→#### Workaround
   398→
   399→If implementing dynamic remapping is complex, a workaround might be to:
   400→- Pre-configure the memory map to the final state
   401→- Patch the table_data reset vector to jump directly to Program ROM's RESET_HANDLER
   402→
   403→However, this violates the project's strict accuracy policy and may cause issues with code that expects the original boot sequence.
   404→
   405→### SubCPU_Send_Payload Details
   406→
   407→The `SubCPU_Send_Payload` routine at **0xEF068A** is responsible for transferring the Sub CPU firmware during boot. This section provides implementation details; see [Inter-CPU Protocol]({{ site.baseurl }}/inter-cpu-protocol/#subcpu_send_payload-0xef068a) for full code examples.
   408→
   409→#### Memory Map State at Execution
   410→
   411→When `SubCPU_Send_Payload` is called, the memory map has been configured by the Stage 1 bootloader with these settings:
   412→
   413→**Memory Controller Configuration (MSAR/MAMR Registers):**
   414→
   415→| Register | Value | Resulting Mapping |
   416→|----------|-------|-------------------|
   417→| MSAR0 | 0x1E | Block 0 starts at 0x1E0000 (SRAM) |
   418→| MSAR1 | 0x10 | Block 1 starts at 0x100000 (I/O) |
   419→| MSAR2 | 0xC0 | Block 2 starts at 0xC00000 |
   420→| MSAR3 | 0x00 | Block 3 starts at 0x000000 (DRAM) |
   421→| MSAR4 | 0x80 | Block 4 starts at 0x800000 (Table Data ROM) |
   422→| MSAR5 | 0x00 | Block 5 starts at 0x000000 |
   423→
   424→**Effective Memory Map:**
   425→
   426→| Address Range | Component | Notes |
   427→|---------------|-----------|-------|
   428→| 0x000000-0x0FFFFF | DRAM (1MB) | Main CPU working RAM |
   429→| 0x100000-0x1DFFFF | I/O Peripherals | FDC, LCD, Latch, etc. |
   430→| 0x1E0000-0x1EFFFF | SRAM | Static RAM |
   431→| 0x300000-0x3FFFFF | Custom Data Flash | External chip select (B1CS) |
   432→| 0x800000-0x9FFFFF | **Table Data ROM** | Contains Sub CPU payload at offset 0x30000 |
   433→| 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF | Program ROM | Currently executing code |
   434→
   435→**Address Resolution for Key Accesses:**
   436→
   437→- **0x830000** → Table Data ROM offset 0x30000 (Sub CPU firmware payload)
   438→- **0x8E0000** → Table Data ROM offset 0xE0000 (LZSS compressed preset data)
   439→- **0x3E0000** → Custom Data Flash offset 0xE0000 (firmware update staging area)
   440→
   441→#### Control Flags
   442→
   443→Two bytes in Program ROM control the payload transfer behavior:
   444→
   445→| Address | ROM Offset | Value | Effect |
   446→|---------|------------|-------|--------|
   447→| 0xFFFEEF | 0x1FFEEF | **0xFF** | Payload transfer proceeds |
   448→| 0xFFFEED | 0x1FFEED | **0xFF** | LZSS decompression is attempted |
   449→
   450→Both flags are 0xFF in the factory ROM, meaning:
   451→1. The full payload transfer executes
   452→2. The LZSS decompression from 0x3E0000 is attempted
   453→
   454→#### Transfer Sequence
   455→
   456→| Step | Source Address | Destination | Size | Notes |
   457→|------|----------------|-------------|------|-------|
   458→| 1-5 | 0x830000-0x870000 | Sub CPU 0x050000-0x090000 | 5 × 64KB | Main payload from Table Data ROM |
   459→| 6 | 0x3E0000 | Decompressed buffer | ~33KB | Optional LZSS preset data (see below) |
   460→| 7 | Buffer + 0x100 | Main CPU 0x0404 | 2 bytes | Copies word to Main CPU RAM |
   461→| 8-10 | Buffer/Fallback | Sub CPU 0x00F000-0x02F000 | 3 × 64KB | Additional data blocks |
   462→| 11 | Buffer | Sub CPU 0x000400 | 256 bytes | Entry point area |
   463→
   464→#### Timing
   465→
   466→The routine includes two delay loops for hardware timing:
   467→- **Initial delay**: 0x2000 iterations (~8,192 cycles) before first transfer
   468→- **Inter-chunk delay**: 0x100000 iterations (~1,048,576 cycles) between chunks
   469→
   470→#### LZSS Preset Data Handling
   471→
   472→After the main 5×64KB payload transfer, the routine attempts to load additional "preset" parameter data:
   473→
   474→**Code Flow:**
   475→```asm
   476→LD XIZ, TABLE_DATA_ROM__BASE_ADDR    ; Default: 0x800000
   477→CP (0xFFFEED), 0xFF                  ; Check decompression flag
   478→JR NZ, skip_decompress               ; Skip if flag != 0xFF
   479→
   480→; Attempt LZSS decompression from Custom Data Flash
   481→LD XIZ, 0x050000                     ; Output buffer (DRAM)
   482→LD XWA, 0x3E0000                     ; Source: Custom Data Flash!
   483→CALL LABEL_EF41E3                    ; Decompress
   484→CP HL, 0xFFFF                        ; Check for failure
   485→JR NZ, skip_decompress               ; Success: use decompressed data
   486→LD XIZ, TABLE_DATA_ROM__BASE_ADDR    ; Failure: fall back to ROM
   487→
   488→skip_decompress:
   489→; Use data at XIZ+0x100 for subsequent transfers
   490→```
   491→
   492→**Key Finding: Address 0x3E0000 is NOT in Table Data ROM**
   493→
   494→The address `0x3E0000` maps to **Custom Data Flash** (0x300000-0x3FFFFF), NOT Table Data ROM. This region is controlled by external chip select logic (B1CS), not the MSAR block memory controller.
   495→
   496→| Address | Maps To | Normal Boot State |
   497→|---------|---------|-------------------|
   498→| 0x3E0000 | Custom Data Flash offset 0xE0000 | User data / empty |
   499→| 0x8E0000 | Table Data ROM offset 0xE0000 | LZSS compressed preset data |
   500→
   501→**Boot Behavior:**
   502→
   503→| Scenario | 0x3E0000 Contents | Decompression | Data Source |
   504→|----------|-------------------|---------------|-------------|
   505→| **After firmware update** | Valid LZSS data | Succeeds | Custom Data Flash (updated firmware) |
   506→| **Factory state** | Empty / user data | Fails (0xFFFF) | Table Data ROM fallback |
   507→
   508→**Firmware Update Integration:**
   509→
   510→The File Type 007 handler (`HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h` at 0xEF47FA) writes compressed Sub CPU payload to Custom Data Flash:
   511→
   512→```asm
   513→; "Technics KN5000 Program DATA FILE PCK"
   514→HANDLE_UPDATE_FILE_TYPE_ID_007h:
   515→    LD WA, 1                    ; Select Custom Data Flash
   516→    LD XBC, 003e0000h           ; Destination: 0x3E0000
   517→    CALL LABEL_EF3929           ; Flash write routine
   518→    LD WA, 1
   519→    LD XBC, 003f0000h           ; Destination: 0x3F0000
   520→    CALL LABEL_EF3929           ; Flash write routine
   521→```
   522→
   523→This explains the design:
   524→1. **Firmware updates** write compressed payload to Custom Data Flash at 0x3E0000
   525→2. **On next boot**, `SubCPU_Send_Payload` decompresses the updated firmware
   526→3. **Factory units** have no data at 0x3E0000, so they fall back to Table Data ROM
   527→
   528→> **✅ RESOLVED:** The 0x3E0000 address mystery is now understood. See [Firmware Update System]({{ site.baseurl }}/lzss-compression/#firmware-update-system-and-0x3e0000) for full details.
   529→
   530→#### Related Routines
   531→
   532→| Routine | Address | Purpose |
   533→|---------|---------|---------|
   534→| `SubCPU_Init_DMA_Channels` | 0xEF329E | Must be called before payload transfer |
   535→| `InterCPU_E1_Bulk_Transfer` | 0xEF3457 | Underlying protocol for each 64KB chunk |
   536→| `SubCPU_Payload_Verify` | 0xEF092B | Verifies payload checksums after transfer |
   537→| `SubCPU_Payload_GetErrorFlag` | 0xEF096A | Returns error status for boot sequence |
   538→
   539→#### Error Handling
   540→
   541→If the payload transfer or verification fails:
   542→1. `SubCPU_Payload_Verify` sets error flag at `0x01E53E`
   543→2. Boot sequence reads flag via `SubCPU_Payload_GetErrorFlag`
   544→3. Non-zero result triggers "ERROR in CPU data transmission" dialog
   545→4. Error dialog defined at `ErrorDialog_CPUTransmissionError` (0xED66BA)
   546→
   547→#### Source Code Reference
   548→
   549→Assembly: `maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm:134212-134295`
   550→
   551→```asm
   552→; Entry point
   553→SubCPU_Send_Payload:                ; 0xEF068A
   554→    PUSH XIZ
   555→    CP (0xFFFEEF), 0xFF              ; Check if transfer should proceed
   556→    JRL NZ, LABEL_EF078B             ; Skip if not 0xFF
   557→    ; ... 5 x 64KB transfers via InterCPU_E1_Bulk_Transfer ...
   558→    ; ... LZSS decompression handling ...
   559→    ; ... Final data blocks to Sub CPU ...
   560→    POP XIZ
   561→    RET
   562→```
   563→
   564→### Subprogram Storage Location (RESOLVED)
   565→
   566→The Sub CPU firmware payload storage is now fully understood:
   567→
   568→**Primary Payload: Table Data ROM offset 0x30000**
   569→
   570→The main Sub CPU firmware (192KB, matching `kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom`) is stored **uncompressed** at:
   571→
   572→| Source | Address | ROM Offset | Size | Destination |
   573→|--------|---------|------------|------|-------------|
   574→| Table Data ROM | 0x830000-0x87FFFF | 0x30000-0x7FFFF | 320KB | Sub CPU 0x050000-0x090000 |
   575→
   576→This is the definitive source of the Sub CPU executable. The `SubCPU_Send_Payload` routine transfers 5×64KB chunks via `InterCPU_E1_Bulk_Transfer`.
   577→
   578→**LZSS Compressed Region at 0x8E0000 (Preset Parameters, NOT Executable):**
   579→
   580→There is SLIDE4K compressed data at Table Data ROM offset 0x0E0000 (address 0x8E0000 after remap):
   581→
   582→```
   583→Address: 0x8E0000 (Table Data ROM, post-remap)
   584→Header:  "SLIDE4K" + 0x00 + 0x00 + 0x95 + 0x00 + "}Z" + 0xEE
   585→Format:  LZSS SLIDE4K compressed
   586→```
   587→
   588→**Important Finding:** This compressed region does **NOT** contain the Sub CPU executable:
   589→- Decompresses to ~33KB of parameter-like data
   590→- Sub CPU ROM (`kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom`) is ~192KB
   591→- Decompressed bytes are mostly MIDI-range values (0-127), not code
   592→
   593→**Address 0x3E0000 Clarification:**
   594→
   595→The code references `0x3E0000` for LZSS decompression, but this address maps to **Custom Data Flash** (not Table Data ROM):
   596→
   597→| Address | Memory Region | Typical Contents |
   598→|---------|---------------|------------------|
   599→| 0x3E0000 | Custom Data Flash (offset 0xE0000) | User data or empty |
   600→| 0x8E0000 | Table Data ROM (offset 0xE0000) | LZSS compressed preset data |
   601→
   602→In normal factory boot, the LZSS decompression from 0x3E0000 likely fails (no valid data in Custom Data Flash), causing the code to fall back to `TABLE_DATA_ROM__BASE_ADDR`.
   603→
   604→**Remaining Open Questions:**
   605→
   606→1. ~~What data is at `0x830000`~~ **RESOLVED:** Sub CPU firmware payload
   607→2. ~~How the ~192KB executable reaches Sub CPU RAM~~ **RESOLVED:** Direct 5×64KB transfers
   608→3. ~~Whether Sub CPU has its own dedicated ROM chip~~ **RESOLVED:** Yes, the Sub CPU Boot ROM (128KB, IC30) contains the boot loader; the 192KB payload is transferred from Table Data ROM
   609→4. **NEW:** What is the purpose of the preset data at 0x8E0000, and when is it used?
   610→5. **NEW:** Under what conditions does the 0x3E0000 LZSS path succeed (firmware update mode)?
   611→

   616→## Sub CPU Boot Sequence
   617→
   618→The sub CPU has a dedicated 128KB boot ROM (`kn5000_subcpu_boot.ic30`) that initializes hardware and waits for the payload.
   619→
   620→### 1. Reset Vector (0xFFFEE0)
   621→
   622→The sub CPU's reset vector jumps to `BOOT_INIT` at `0xFF8290`.
   623→
   624→### 2. Hardware Initialization (BOOT_INIT)
   625→
   626→```
   627→Address: 0xFF8290
   628→Size: ~400 bytes
   629→```
   630→
   631→**Initialization steps:**
   632→
   633→| Step | Registers | Values | Purpose |
   634→|------|-----------|--------|---------|
   635→| 1 | WDMOD_REAL | 0x00 | Disable watchdog |
   636→| 2 | INT_CTRL | 0x04 | Configure interrupts |
   637→| 3 | P0FC-P2FC | 0xFF | Port 0-2 all function mode |
   638→| 4 | P7, P7FC, P7CR | Various | Port 7 configuration |
   639→| 5 | P8, P8FC, P8CR | Various | Port 8 (chip select) |
   640→| 6 | PA, PAFC, PB, PBFC | Various | DRAM signals |
   641→| 7 | INTTC01 | 0x03 | Timer interrupt control |
   642→| 8 | SC0/SC1 registers | Various | Serial configuration |
   643→| 9 | T01MOD, T23MOD | Various | Timer modes |
   644→| 10 | MSARx, MAMRx | Various | Memory controller |
   645→| 11 | SER0/SER1 | Various | Serial channels |
   646→| 12 | DRAM_* | Various | DRAM refresh/timing |
   647→| 13 | BxCSL, BxCSH | Various | Bus chip select |
   648→
   649→### 3. Copy Interrupt Vectors (Boot_Copy_Vectors)
   650→
   651→```
   652→Address: 0xFF846D
   653→Source: 0xFF8F6C (ROM)
   654→Destination: 0x0400 (RAM)
   655→Size: 225 bytes (0xE1 bytes)
   656→```
   657→
   658→The boot ROM copies interrupt vector trampolines from ROM to RAM. These are placeholder handlers that jump back to boot ROM until the actual payload overwrites them:
   659→
   660→```asm
   661→Boot_Copy_Vectors:             ; 0xFF846D
   662→    LD   XDE, 0x00000400       ; Destination: RAM at 0x0400
   663→    LD   XHL, 0x00FF8F6C       ; Source: ROM stub table
   664→    LD   XBC, 0x000000E1       ; Count: 225 bytes
   665→    LDIR                       ; Block copy
   666→    RET
   667→```
   668→
   669→### 4. Enable Interrupts
   670→
   671→```asm
   672→ei 0    ; Enable interrupts at level 0
   673→```
   674→
   675→### 5. Initialization Routines
   676→
   677→| Routine | Address | Size | Purpose |
   678→|---------|---------|------|---------|
   679→| INIT_MEMORY_TEST | 0xFF8956 | ~300B | RAM test, ROM checksum |
   680→| INIT_DMA_SERIAL | 0xFF85AE | ~90B | DMA and serial setup |
   681→| INIT_TONE_GEN | 0xFF84A8 | ~70B | Tone generator at 0x130000 |
   682→
   683→### 6. Main Loop (Wait for Payload)
   684→
   685→```
   686→Address: 0xFF8405
   687→```
   688→
   689→The sub CPU enters a loop waiting for the payload ready flag:
   690→
   691→```asm
   692→MAIN_LOOP:
   693→    res  6, (SUBCPU_STATUS_FLAGS)    ; Clear ready flag
   694→.wait_loop:
   695→    bit  6, (SUBCPU_STATUS_FLAGS)    ; Check if payload ready
   696→    jr   Z, .check_status
   697→    ei   6                            ; Enable interrupt level 6
   698→    call PAYLOAD_ENTRY               ; Call payload at 0x0400
   699→.check_status:
   700→    ; Update serial status
   701→    jr   .wait_loop
   702→```
   703→
   704→### 7. Payload Execution
   705→
   706→Once `PAYLOAD_LOADED_FLAG` bit 6 is set (by E3 command), the sub CPU jumps to the payload entry point at `0x0400`. The payload takes over audio synthesis and tone generation duties.

   710→## Inter-CPU Communication Protocol
   711→
   712→The main CPU and sub CPU communicate via a single-byte latch at `0x120000`.
   713→
   714→### Command Format
   715→
   716→| Command | Description | Data Size | Buffer |
   717→|---------|-------------|-----------|--------|
   718→| 0x00-0x1F | Variable-length data | Low 5 bits + 1 | CMD_DATA_BUFFER |
   719→| 0xE1 | Two-phase transfer setup | 6 bytes | CMD_E1_BUFFER |
   720→| 0xE2 | Parameter block | 10 bytes | CMD_E2_BUFFER |
   721→| 0xE3 | Payload complete | 0 bytes | - |
   722→
   723→### Variable-Length Commands (0x00-0x1F)
   724→
   725→```
   726→Bits 7-5: Handler index (0-7) from jump table at 0xFF8000
   727→Bits 4-0: Data length - 1 (so 0x00 = 1 byte, 0x1F = 32 bytes)
   728→```
   729→
   730→### Handshaking Signals (INTERCPU_STATUS at 0x34)
   731→
   732→| Bit | Direction | Meaning |
   733→|-----|-----------|---------|
   734→| 0 | Sub → Main | Sub CPU ready flag |
   735→| 1 | Internal | Completion signal from interrupt |
   736→| 2 | Internal | Gate for command processing |
   737→| 4 | Main → Sub | Main CPU ready flag |
   738→
   739→### DMA State Machine (DMA_XFER_STATE at 0x0516)
   740→
   741→| State | Meaning |
   742→|-------|---------|
   743→| 0 | Idle - no transfer in progress |
   744→| 1 | Single transfer - waiting for completion |
   745→| 2 | Two-phase transfer - phase 1 done, phase 2 pending |
   746→
   747→### Transfer Flow
   748→
   749→```
   750→Main CPU                          Sub CPU
   751→   │                                 │
   752→   │  1. Write command to latch      │
   753→   │  ─────────────────────────────► │
   754→   │                                 │  2. InterCPU_RX_Handler
   755→   │                                 │     triggered
   756→   │                                 │
   757→   │  3. Wait for sub ready          │  4. Set up DMA
   758→   │  ◄───────────────────────────── │     destination
   759→   │                                 │
   760→   │  5. Send data bytes             │
   761→   │  ─────────────────────────────► │  6. DMA receives data
   762→   │                                 │
   763→   │  7. Check completion            │  8. DMA_Complete_Handler
   764→   │  ◄───────────────────────────── │     clears state
   765→   │                                 │
   766→```
   767→

   852→
   853→### Boot Time Estimates
   854→
   855→| Phase | Duration | Notes |
   856→|-------|----------|-------|
   857→| Hardware init | ~1ms | SFR configuration |
   858→| Memory test | ~10ms | RAM pattern test |
   859→| ROM checksum | ~5ms | 4KB verification |
   860→| Tone gen init | ~1ms | 4 channel setup |

   864→### DMA Transfer Rates
   865→
   866→- Latch clock: Tied to timer frequency
   867→- Typical chunk size: 32 bytes
   868→- Timeout: 60,000 iterations (~300ms at 20MHz)

   872→## Error Handling
   873→
   874→### Memory Test Errors (MEMTEST_RESULT)
   875→
   876→| Bit | Meaning |
   877→|-----|---------|
   878→| 0-1 | Low word RAM errors |
   879→| 2-3 | High word RAM errors |
   880→| 3 | ROM checksum mismatch |
   881→
   882→### DMA Timeouts
   883→
   884→All DMA routines have 60,000 iteration timeouts (~300ms). On timeout:
   885→- Transfer is abandoned
   886→- Ready flag is set
   887→- Control returns to caller
   888→
   889→### HALT_LOOP (0xFF8490)
   890→
   891→Fatal error handler that disables serial and halts the CPU:
   892→
   893→```asm
   894→HALT_LOOP:
   895→    res  0, (SC0MOD)    ; Disable serial
   896→.halt:
   897→    halt                ; Halt CPU
   898→    jr   T, .halt       ; Loop forever
   899→```
   900→
   901→---
   902→
   903→## HD-AE5000 Initialization (Optional)
   904→
   905→If the HD-AE5000 hard disk expansion is detected (PE port bit 0 = 0), the main CPU calls its initialization routines.
   906→
   907→### Detection and Entry
   908→
   909→```
   910→Main CPU checks PE.0
   911→    │
   912→    ├─► PE.0 = 1: No HD-AE5000, skip
   913→    │
   914→    └─► PE.0 = 0: HD-AE5000 present
   915→            │
   916→            ▼
   917→        Validate ROM header at 0x280000
   918→        Check for "XAPR" magic string
   919→            │
   920→            ▼
   921→        CALL 0x280008 (Boot Init entry)
   922→```
   923→
   924→### HDAE5000_Boot_Init (0x28F576)
   925→
   926→The boot initialization performs these steps:
   927→
   928→| Step | Action | Details |
   929→|------|--------|---------|
   930→| 1 | Store workspace | Save main CPU workspace pointer at 0x23A1A2 |
   931→| 2 | Clear work buffer | Zero 62KB at 0x22A000 |
   932→| 3 | Register handlers | Register 12 callback handlers with main CPU |
   933→| 4 | Load palette | Load 256-entry VGA palette from ROM |
   934→| 5 | Copy VRAM data | Copy 76,800 bytes to 0x1A0000 and 0x1A9600 |
   935→| 6 | Init handler pointers | Store function pointers at 0x230ECC/ED2/ED6 |
   936→| 7 | RAM test | Fill/verify 32KB at 0x230F1C-0x238F1C |
   937→| 8 | Check HD presence | Detect hard disk, store result at 0x230EDA |
   938→| 9 | Register frame handler | Set up periodic update callback |
   939→
   940→### Workspace Dispatch System
   941→
   942→The main CPU provides a callback registration system that HDAE5000 uses to integrate with the UI framework:
   943→
   944→```
   945→WORKSPACE_PTR (0x23A1A2)
   946→    │
   947→    └──► Handler Table A (offset +0x0E0A)
   948→              │
   949→              ├──► Registration func (offset +0x00E4)
   950→              ├──► Display callback (offset +0x0124)
   951→              ├──► UI callbacks (offsets +0x0244, +0x0248, etc.)
   952→              │
   953→    └──► Handler Table B (offset +0x0E88)
   954→              │
   955→              └──► Audio/system callbacks
   956→```
   957→
   958→HDAE5000 registers 12 handlers using this system, each identified by a port address (0x0160000x) and handler ID.
   959→
   960→### Frame Handler (0x28F662)
   961→
   962→After initialization, the main CPU calls the frame handler periodically:
   963→
   964→1. Calculate display offset from handler states
   965→2. Check for state changes via callback dispatch
   966→3. Monitor status bit 2 for display refresh triggers
   967→4. Jump to PPORT handler for parallel port polling
   968→
   969→---
   970→
   971→## Subsystem Initialization Order
   972→
   973→After boot completes, subsystems initialize in this order:
   974→
   975→```
   976→Sub CPU Payload Loaded (E3 command)
   977→    │
   978→    ▼
   979→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   980→│         Main CPU Subsystem Init             │
   981→├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   982→│  1. Display System (VGA controller)         │
   983→│     - Configure MN89304 at 0x170000         │
   984→│     - Set 320×240 resolution                │
   985→│     - Load default palette                  │
   986→│                                             │
   987→│  2. Control Panel (Serial Channel 1)        │
   988→│     - 250kHz clock, 8-bit mode              │
   989→│     - Initialize button/encoder states      │
   990→│     - Start polling loop                    │
   991→│                                             │
   992→│  3. Floppy Disk Controller (0x110000)       │
   993→│     - Detect drive presence                 │
   994→│     - Initialize FDC state machine          │
   995→│                                             │
   996→│  4. HDAE5000 (if present)                   │
   997→│     - Call 0x280008 for initialization      │
   998→│     - Register frame handler                │
   999→│                                             │
  1000→│  5. MIDI I/O                                │
  1001→│     - Configure serial channels             │
  1002→│     - Initialize message buffers            │
  1003→└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  1004→    │
  1005→    ▼
  1006→    Main Event Loop
  1007→```
  1008→
  1009→---
  1010→
  1011→## System Runtime
  1012→
  1013→### Main Event Loop
  1014→
  1015→After all initialization completes, the main CPU enters its event loop:
  1016→
  1017→```
  1018→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  1019→│                    MAIN EVENT LOOP                        │
  1020→├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  1021→│                                                          │
  1022→│  ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐  │
  1023→│  │   Control   │    │   Display   │    │    MIDI     │  │
  1024→│  │   Panel     │───►│   Update    │───►│  Processing │  │
  1025→│  │   Poll      │    │             │    │             │  │
  1026→│  └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘  │
  1027→│         │                  │                  │          │
  1028→│         ▼                  ▼                  ▼          │
  1029→│  ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐  │
  1030→│  │    FDC      │    │  HDAE5000   │    │   Audio     │  │
  1031→│  │   Handler   │───►│   Frame     │───►│   Sync      │  │
  1032→│  │             │    │   Handler   │    │             │  │
  1033→│  └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘  │
  1034→│                           │                              │
  1035→│                           ▼                              │
  1036→│                    Loop continues                        │
  1037→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  1038→```
  1039→
  1040→### Control Panel Communication
  1041→
  1042→The control panel uses a serial protocol at 250kHz:
  1043→
  1044→| Direction | Data | Purpose |
  1045→|-----------|------|---------|
  1046→| Main → Panel | Button LED states | Update indicator LEDs |
  1047→| Panel → Main | Button presses | User input events |
  1048→| Panel → Main | Encoder deltas | Rotary encoder changes |
  1049→
  1050→See [Control Panel Protocol]({{ site.baseurl }}/control-panel-protocol/) for detailed protocol documentation.
  1051→
  1052→### Inter-CPU Communication (Runtime)
  1053→
  1054→During runtime, the main CPU sends commands to the sub CPU for audio operations:
  1055→
  1056→| Command Range | Purpose |
  1057→|---------------|---------|
  1058→| 0x00-0x1F | DSP/audio control |
  1059→| 0x20-0x3F | Audio parameters |
  1060→| 0x40-0x5F | Tone generator |
  1061→| 0x60-0x7F | Effects processing |
  1062→| 0x80-0x9F | Serial port setup |
  1063→| 0xA0-0xBF | Voice commands |
  1064→| 0xC0-0xFF | System commands |
  1065→
  1066→### HDAE5000 PPORT Polling
  1067→
  1068→If HD-AE5000 is present, its frame handler checks for PC parallel port commands:
  1069→
  1070→1. Check PPORT status register at 0x239000
  1071→2. If active, load parameters from 0x23900A-0x239010
  1072→3. Call PPORT_Setup (0x29511C) and PPORT_Dispatch (0x2950CC)
  1073→4. Process command from jump table at 0x2953E2
  1074→
  1075→Available PPORT commands include file transfers, HD formatting, and PC communication.
  1076→
  1077→---
  1078→
  1079→## Complete Boot Timeline

  1081→```

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive view of the DRAM memory mapping. Let me compile my findings.

## KN5000 DRAM Memory Mapping Analysis

Based on my analysis of the documentation, original boot code, and your minimal version, here are my findings:

### 1. **DRAM Address Range and Mapping**

**DRAM is mapped to Block 3:** `0x000000 - 0x0FFFFF` (1MB of the 32-bit address space)

This is controlled by the Memory Address Start Register (MSAR) and Memory Address Mask Register (MAMR):

| Register | Value | Result |
|----------|-------|--------|
| **MSAR3** | `0x00` | Block 3 starts at **0x000000** |
| **MAMR3** | `0x1F` | Block 3 address mask (defines block size) |

**The mask value 0x1F decodes to:**
- Binary: `00011111`
- Creates a 1MB block (bits 19-0 are address bits, bits 20+ are block select)
- **Final range: 0x000000 - 0x0FFFFF**

**Important note about 0x200000:** The address 0x200000 you asked about is **NOT** in the main DRAM block. According to the memory map documentation, there's conflicting information:
- The memory-map.md shows VRAM at `0x1A0000 - 0x1A7FFF` (512KB)
- References to 0x200000 appear in disassembled code but may refer to different hardware (or be documentation artifacts)
- The actual working RAM for your VM should be in the **0x000000 - 0x0FFFFF range**

### 2. **DRAM Controller Registers Configuration**

All three boot versions (original, your minimal version) use **identical DRAM controller settings**:


; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>
; Licensed under GPL version 2 or later.
;
; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
;
; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
;
; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
; as a high-level emulation on MAME
;
; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
;
; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
;
; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
; using the scripts provided at:
; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
;
; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh

CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte

FROZEN	EQU 0
NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh

; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h

; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0C5h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0DCh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0E9h
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FAh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FBh
VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FBh
VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h

; Game part IDs
GAME_PART_INTRO			EQU 03E80h
NUM_MEM_LIST			EQU 091h

CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN:
	; int16_t xmax = MAX(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP GT, XMAX_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMAX_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMAX), WA
	
	; int16_t xmin = MIN(x1, x2);
	LD WA, (X1)
	CP WA, (X2)
	JP LT, XMIN_OK
	LD WA, (X2)
XMIN_OK:
	LD (LINE_XMIN), WA
	RET

drawLineN:
	; Inputs:
	; C = color
	PUSH XIX
	PUSH XHL
	
	CALL CALC_LINE_XMAX_AND_XMIN

	; for (int16_t x=xmin; x<=xmax; x++)
	; 	m_curPagePtr1->pix(m_hliney, x) = color;
	LD XIX, (CUR_LINE)
	ADDW (CUR_LINE_LOW), 320
	ADCW (CUR_LINE_HIGH), 0
	LD HL, (LINE_XMIN)
	EXTS XHL
	ADD XIX, XHL
	LD HL, (LINE_XMAX)
	SUB HL, (LINE_XMIN)

drawLineN_loop:
	LDB (XIX), C
	INC XIX
	DJNZ HL, drawLineN_loop
	
	POP XHL

content.text:
Here is the complete memory map for the KN5000 as configured in the MAME driver.

---

## Main CPU (TMP94C241F) Memory Map

From `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp`, function `kn5000_state::maincpu_mem`:

| Address Range | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `0x000000 - 0x0FFFFF` | RAM | 1MB DRAM (2x 4Mbit), shared as `nvram1` (CS3) |
| `0x110000 - 0x11FFFF` | I/O | Floppy Controller (uPD765A) -- **not yet mapped (FIXME)** |
| `0x120000 - 0x12FFFF` | I/O | Floppy DMA Acknowledge -- **not yet mapped (FIXME)** |
| `0x140000 - 0x14FFFF` | I/O | Inter-CPU latch: Read from maincpu_latch (IC23), Write to subcpu_latch (IC22) |
| `0x1703B0 - 0x1703DF` | I/O | VGA I/O registers (`mn89304_vga_device::io_map`, LCD controller IC206) |
| `0x1A0000 - 0x1DFFFF` | RAM | VRAM, 256KB linear framebuffer (VGA `mem_linear_r`/`mem_linear_w`) |
| `0x1E0000 - 0x1FFFFF` | RAM | 128KB SRAM (IC21, CS0), shared as `nvram2` -- backup SRAM |
| `0x300000 - 0x3FFFFF` | ROM | 1MB Custom Data Flash ROM (IC19, CS5) |
| `0x400000 - 0x7FFFFF` | ROM | 4MB Rhythm Data ROM (IC14, A22=1 and CS5) |
| `0x800000 - 0x9FFFFF` | ROM | 2MB Table Data (2x 8Mbit ROMs, IC1/IC3, CS2), mirrored at `0xA00000-0xBFFFFF` |
| `0xE00000 - 0xFFFFFF` | ROM | 2MB Program ROM (2x 8Mbit Flash, IC4/IC6), masked to 0x1FFFFF |

### Extension Board Overlay (HD-AE5000)

The extension board's `card_map` is installed into the main CPU address space at `machine_start()` via `m_extension->program_map(m_maincpu->space(AS_PROGRAM))`. From `/home/fsanches/devel/kn5000-roms-disasm/mame_driver/src/devices/bus/technics/kn5000/hdae5000.cpp`, function `hdae5000_device::card_map`:

| Address Range | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `0x130010 - 0x130011` | I/O | ATA Data Register (16-bit R/W) |
| `0x130012 - 0x13001F` | I/O | ATA registers (Error/Features, Sector Count, CHS, Status/Command) |
| `0x130020 - 0x130021` | I/O | ATA Device Control (write only) |
| `0x160000 - 0x160007` | I/O | PPI (NEC uPD71055/i8255) parallel port for PC communication |
| `0x200000 - 0x27FFFF` | RAM | 512KB Static RAM (2x 256KB chips) |
| `0x280000 - 0x2FFFFF` | ROM | 512KB Extension ROM |

### Key observations

1. **VRAM is 256KB** (`0x1A0000-0x1DFFFF`), not 512KB as stated in the project's CLAUDE.md. The CLAUDE.md says "512KB VRAM at 0x1A0000" but the MAME driver maps only 256KB (0x40000 bytes).

2. **The extension board's RAM at `0x200000-0x27FFFF`** overlaps nothing in the base map -- there is a gap between SRAM at `0x1FFFFF` and custom data ROM at `0x300000`.

3. **VGA I/O ports** are at `0x1703B0-0x1703DF`, not at `0x170000` as the docs suggest. The DAC palette registers (typically VGA port `0x3C8`/`0x3C9`) would be mapped at `0x1703C8`/`0x1703C9` within the VGA `io_map`.

4. **RAM at `0x000000`** is a full 1MB DRAM region. The Another World VM uses `0x200000` for its RAM and `0x240000-0x270000` for page buffers -- these fall into the extension board's 512KB SRAM when the HD-AE5000 is present, or are unmapped without it.

---

## Sub CPU Memory Map

From `kn5000_state::subcpu_mem`:

| Address Range | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `0x000000 - 0x0FFFFF` | RAM | 1MB DRAM (IC28/IC29) |
| `0x110000 - 0x11????` | I/O | Tone Generator (IC303) -- **not yet mapped** |
| `0x120000 - 0x12FFFF` | I/O | Inter-CPU latch: Read from subcpu_latch (IC22), Write to maincpu_latch (IC23) |
| `0x130000 - 0x13????` | I/O | DSP1 (IC311) -- **not yet mapped** |
| `0xFE0000 - 0xFFFFFF` | ROM | 128KB Sub CPU Mask ROM (IC30) |

DSP2 (IC302) uses serial port 0 pins (likely bit-banged).

	rept 0F0000h		; ~960KB of padding
	db 0FFh
	endm

	ORG 0EF0000h

; Jump to Reset_Handler (VGA code is included first for macro definitions)
	jp Reset_Handler

; Include shared VGA I/O and initialization routines
	include "vga_io.asm"
	include "vga_init.asm"
	ret			; VGA_Setup has no ret (designed for inline use)

; Entry Point - Called after hardware reset
Reset_Handler:
	include "boot_hw_init.asm"

	; Set up stack pointer (after hardware init)
	LDA_XWA_IMM24 STACK_TOP
	ld XSP, XWA

	; Initialize VGA display using shared code
	CALR VGA_Setup

	; Turn screen on (sequencer clocking mode)
	VGA_SEQUENCER 01h, 001h

	jp ENTRY

	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU

; =============================================================================
; Extension Board ROM Layout
; =============================================================================
	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION

	ORG 0280000h

EXTENSION_HEADER:
	db 'XAPR'
	dd POINTERS
	JP ENTRY
POINTERS:
	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE

	endif ; TARGET_EXTENSION

; =============================================================================
; VM Code (shared between both targets)
; =============================================================================
	include "another_world_vm.asm"

; =============================================================================
; ROM End (target-specific)
; =============================================================================
	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU

Default_Handler:
	halt
	jr Default_Handler

; Reset Handler Location
	ORG 0FFFEE0h
Reset_Entry:
	jp Reset_Handler

; Fill gap between reset entry and vector table
	ORG 0FFFEE4h
	rept 01Ch
	db 0FFh
	endm

; Interrupt Vector Table
	ORG 0FFFF00h
VECTOR_TABLE:
	dd 00FFFEE0h		; Vector 0: Reset
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 1
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 2
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 3
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 4
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 5
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 6
	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 7

	rept 56
	dd Default_Handler
	endm

	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU

	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION

	ORG 02FFFFFh
	db 0FFh

	endif ; TARGET_EXTENSION

; =============================================================================
; End of ROM
; =============================================================================
	end

+OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1	EQU 060000h	; Offscreen buffer (required by vga_init, in DRAM)
